title: Frisia Kingdom
capsule: The Frisian kingdom (Magna Frisia) stretched along the North Sea coast and Rhine delta from roughly the Scheldt to the Weser, coalescing into a recognizable polity in the 7th century under kings such as Aldgisl and Radbod (Redbad). Its rulers controlled the wealthy trading emporium of Dorestad and the lower Rhine, and Radbod repelled Frankish encroachment for a time, exploiting instability after the death of Pepin of Herstal in 714 to recover ground around the old Rhine frontier. Radbod's death in 719 removed the kingdom's most effective leader and marked the high point of independent Frisian power; thereafter Frankish pressure under the Carolingians steadily eroded Frisian autonomy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Frisian kingdom's political core is attested in Frankish chronicles and hagiographic sources, but its territorial extent is poorly defined; archaeological evidence suggests the 'kingdom' comprised several loosely associated petty chieftaincies rather than a unified polity.
